correctness.rationale: The two-term derangement recurrence and alternating parity give v2(D_m)=v2(m-1) for odd m>=3. The factorial identity leaves only odd divisors m and m-2 in the denominator, proving the full binary formula; m=3 attains the minimum. With N=n-3, Lucas gives precisely the even submasks j<N of N. When N is odd they omit the low bit and are automatically proper; when N is even exclude only N. For an odd p<=n outside a pure p-power row, take m=p^j at a nonzero positive-position digit of n: both factors are p-units by Lucas and the derangement recurrence modulo p. Primes p>n are excluded by m=3. On n=p^a every selected binomial coefficient is divisible by p; the m=p^(a-1) coefficient has exactly one base-p carry and a p-unit weight for a>=2. This includes n=9, m=3: the proof's phrase 'strictly between 3 and n' is an endpoint slip, since 3 is admissible. For a=1, m=3 gives exactly exponent one. Independent inclusion–exclusion produced derangements and checked 1,675 exact assertions on n=4..80 (after a 43-assertion pilot), including each binary valuation and the minimizing columns.
residual_risks: The exact integer replay is finite; the recurrence, factorial identity and digit arguments give the unrestricted conclusion.
